notes: The ADR-003 content-only RecoveryRecord, pinned across Go, Java and Swift. Argon2id (v1.3) then ChaCha20-Poly1305 (IETF, 12-byte nonce) with the authenticated header - magic, version, work factors and salt - as associated data. Salt and nonce are FIXED here; a real export draws both fresh, which is why the vectors pin inputs rather than an output of Export. The negative set carries both attacks the format is shaped around: downgrade (claim cheap work factors) and inflation (claim absurd ones and let the reader allocate them). Cases flagged reject_before_derivation must be refused from the header alone.

derivation.name: register_defaults
derivation.description: The register's frozen work factors: 64 MiB, 3 passes, one lane.

derivation.name: register_minima
derivation.description: The weakest parameters an import still accepts. The boundary is inclusive, so an implementation that wrote > where it meant >= fails here rather than in the field.

derivation.name: empty_passphrase
derivation.description: Argon2id accepts a zero-length password. Pinned because a binding that rejects it, or that silently substitutes something, would otherwise surface only as an unopenable record for the one user who did it.

derivation.name: non_ascii_passphrase
derivation.description: A passphrase with characters outside ASCII, as UTF-8. Not decoration: the obvious Swift binding for crypto_pwhash maps the password bytes through Int8(_:), which TRAPS on any byte above 0x7F - a crash, not an error, for every user whose passphrase has an accent in it.

positive.name: defaults_roundtrip
positive.description: An ordinary export at the register's defaults. Sealing must reproduce these exact bytes from these exact inputs; opening must return the content.

positive.name: empty_content
positive.description: A record sealing nothing. The ciphertext is the tag alone, which is the length arithmetic most likely to be wrong on a platform that assumed a non-empty plaintext.

positive.name: register_minima_accepted
positive.description: An authentic record written at the minima. It must OPEN, not merely validate - the pair to downgrade_authentic_weak_record below, which is one step weaker and must be refused.

negative.name: downgrade_memory_below_minimum
negative.description: The header rewritten to claim 8 KiB. Refused on the register minimum, before the cheap derivation the attacker was shopping for.

negative.name: downgrade_iterations_below_minimum
negative.description: The header rewritten to claim a single pass.

negative.name: downgrade_authentic_weak_record
negative.description: Not an edit: a record genuinely SEALED at 8 KiB and one pass, so the AEAD verifies and only the minima check stands between the user and a backup worth guessing at. This is the case a tamper check alone would pass.

negative.name: downgrade_within_bounds_fails_authentication
negative.description: The subtle half. The header is rewritten from 64 MiB to the 32 MiB minimum - still legal parameters, so the bounds check has nothing to say. What refuses it is that the work factors are AEAD associated data: the edited header derives a different key AND authenticates different bytes, so the attacker gets a failure rather than a cheaper guess.

negative.name: inflation_memory_above_ceiling
negative.description: The header rewritten to demand 8 GiB. One flipped bit in this field turns 64 MiB into 16 GiB, and a reader that derives before it validates hangs or is OOM-killed - denial of service for anyone who can hand the user a file.

negative.name: inflation_memory_uint32_max
negative.description: The memory field set to the largest value it can hold. It is here for the sign bit rather than the size: a reader that holds this field in a SIGNED 32-bit integer sees -1, which is below every ceiling and above nothing, so a ceiling check written the obvious way lets it through. Reject it, and reject it as a parameter rejection rather than by accident.

negative.name: inflation_iterations_uint32_max
negative.description: The same sign trap in the time-cost field.

negative.name: inflation_iterations_above_ceiling
negative.description: The same attack in the time dimension: passes beyond the absolute ceiling.

negative.name: inflation_parallelism_unsupported
negative.description: Two lanes. libsodium's crypto_pwhash has no multi-lane entry point and it is the binding on both shipping platforms, so a two-lane record would open in Go and nowhere a user could use it. All three refuse it identically.

negative.name: wrong_passphrase
negative.description: The everyday failure. It must be reported with the same code and the same detail as a tampered record: telling them apart is an oracle (TRS-CRY-013).

negative.name: salt_edited
negative.description: A byte of the salt flipped. The salt is inside the associated data, so this fails authentication rather than quietly deriving from a different salt.

negative.name: foreign_magic
negative.description: A file that is not a record at all. Refused on the magic, without a passphrase prompt and without reading further.

negative.name: unknown_format_version
negative.description: A record claiming a layout this build does not know. Refused rather than parsed optimistically.

negative.name: truncated_to_header
negative.description: Everything after the header removed. There is no ciphertext to open and no tag to check.

negative.name: truncated_mid_header
negative.description: A record shorter than its own header. A reader that indexes before it length-checks crashes here instead of returning an error.
